title: kv-thrashing-rootcause-hypothesis-and-mini-bench-report
content:
Summary:
This note is a working write-up of an odd production pattern we've been seeing for the last 2 weeks: repeated microburst tail-latency spikes on a subset of Dedicated nodes tied to sudden increases in NVMe read/write rates and concurrent high eviction churn in the KV cache. The bursts are short (200-800ms), recur at 10-30s intervals for impacted nodes, and correlate with small-request, mixed-seqlen workloads. Goal here is to capture hypotheses, a compact bench to reproduce, quick numbers, and next remediation ideas we can iterate on.

Context / why this feels different:
- We've seen eviction-driven tail before, but this pattern has: a) tight periodicity, b) simultaneous outbound NVMe saturation + PCIe spikes, and c) eviction churn that seems to oscillate rather than settle.
- Affected stacks: mostly A100s with NVMe tier configured as spillback for large KV footprints; also observed on one VPC private deployment.
- Rollouts/fallouts: customer impact = higher p95/p99 token latency, occasional request timeouts in worst cases. No data loss.

Observed signals (prod traces & perf counters):
- Telemetry window snapshot (one event):
  - time: 2025-11-02T13:17:34Z
  - node: dedicated-a100-12
  - 99th token latency: 920ms (baseline 85ms)
  - NVMe read rate: +18 GB/s spike for 320ms
  - PCIe utilization: jump from 28%->82% coincident with NVMe spike
  - KV evict/sec: 11k (steady-state ~800)
  - resident-set size: 78% -> 41% within 450ms (rapid evict)
  - concurrent inflight requests: 62 -> 19 (SLA-triggered short-circuit)

Initial hypothesis set (ranked):
1) Cross-tenant burst alignment + eviction hysteresis: multiple tenants' long-prefix misses coincide causing coordinated prefetch/evict waves. Evictor overshoots due to stale hotness signals and then oscillates (positive feedback).
2) NVMe controller QoS / write amplification interplay: heavy eviction writes to NVMe cause internal GC which temporarily reduces read bandwidth and increases PCIe churn, amplifying read latency for the next wave.
3) Host-side scheduling / async IO backlog: the IO worker threads hit a pathological scheduling jitter under certain load mixes (many small reads + occasional large sequential spillbacks) causing bursts of batched NVMe flushes.
4) KV metadata contention path: lock contention in the residency manager during simultaneous eviction + lookup storms causing stalls and delayed reclaim, which then produces a spike when a background thread flushes a big chunk.

Why we think (1) is most likely:
- Correlation across tenants observed in traces (tenant set A + B had aligned heavy prefix misses).
- When we artificially staggered request arrival (test harness), oscillation amplitude dropped markedly.
- Evict/sec curve shows a classic underdamped response (overshoot then inverse correction) consistent with hysteresis in priority / aging heuristics.

Mini-bench to reproduce (how-to):
- Purpose: get a small, reproducible local lab trace that exhibits the same periodic eviction/NVMe spike behavior so we can iterate fixes faster.
- Hardware: 2x A100 (dev cluster), NVMe 4TB, kernel 6.x (same as prod image)
- Binary/branch: serving-runtime:kv-thrash-harness (local branch), run harness with small modifications below.
- Workload pattern: 3 tenants; tenant A: synthetic chat mix (seqlen 128, high prefix variance); tenant B: search-rerank batch (short seqlens, high qps bursts); tenant C: background cache-warm traffic (steady low qps).
- Arrival pattern: align bursts for A & B (burst length 6s, rest 24s) to emulate observed 10-30s periodicity.
- KV config: resident limit 64GB, spillback enabled, prefetch disabled, eviction policy = LRU+priority-aging (current prod config).
- Tracing flags: enable io-trace, evictor-trace, scheduler-trace at DEBUG for 3 min runs.

Mini-bench results (one representative run):
- run length: 3m30s
- observed periodicity: 26s (matches prod window)
- peak NVMe read rate: 16.7 GB/s for 380ms windows
- average evict/sec during bursts: 9.2k, baseline outside bursts: 640
- resident-set swing: 66% -> 38% -> 70% over cycle
- measured reuse-rate (hot-key reuse within 60s window): dropped from 0.71 -> 0.19 during bursts (large churn)
- CPU impact: io-worker CPU spike correlated with PCIe interrupts (1.8x user+sys)
- Lock profiling (flamegraph): residency-manager lock held 11.6% of wall time during spike vs 0.9% baseline

Interpreting numbers / signal synthesis:
- The bench reproduces the oscillation and NVMe spikes reliably with aligned bursts.
- Reuse collapse indicates eviction chasing a moving working set — consistent with hypothesis (1).
- Lock hold-time increase suggests there is a metadata path that becomes hot during the burst; this can exaggerate latency by serializing access and delaying prefetch/evict work.
- NVMe read/write spikes are likely a downstream consequence (evictor writes + spillback reads), not the root cause, but they amplify the client-visible tail.

Quick experiments tried (notes):
- Staggering bursts by 2s across tenants: amplitude down ~60%, p99 back to ~180ms.
- Turning off spillback (force in-memory only): reduced NVMe spike but still saw eviction oscillation (smaller amplitude) — indicates spillback amplifies but doesn't originate the oscillation.
- Increase eviction hysteresis (double priority aging window): lowered evict/sec peak by ~35% but increased baseline memory utilization; p99 improved marginally.
- Add per-tenant eviction caps (local to evictor): eliminated oscillation in bench but caused unfairness in some tenants (starvation in synthetic warmers).

Shortlist of candidate fixes (fast -> longer term):
- Fast (lab -> can prod canary in 1 week):
  * Add jitter to eviction/priority-aging wakeups so multiple tenants' evictors don't align (low risk).
  * Add heuristic: if eviction rate crosses threshold and reuse-rate drops rapidly, temporarily pause background bulk-evict and switch to conservative per-request reclaim for 1-2s.
- Medium:
  * Per-tenant admission controller (soft cap + backpressure) to avoid synchronized large working-set misses.
  * Improve residency-manager lock granularity (split metadata shards) to reduce serialized hold time in bursts.
- Long run / Research:
  * Model-based evictor (control-theory PID-ish) to dampen oscillations automatically based on reuse-rate and resident swing.
  * NVMe-aware eviction pacing that keeps a sliding budget for NVMe I/O to avoid triggering controller GC cycles.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we instrument tenant alignment at the router layer to detect/auto-stagger bursts earlier? (Derek)
- Is there any kernel-level NVMe telemetry we can surface to help correlate controller GC events with our spikes? (Priya)
- Quick safety check: do any eviction jitter mitigations risk increased p50/p75 latency? run micro-SLA tests. (Jonah)
- Run the bench with a different eviction policy (CLOCK-Pro variant) to see if oscillation is policy-specific. (Maya)

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Ship small bench harness and run in staged perf lab across two more hardware variants (done: A100 x1; todo: other GPU + different NVMe makes).
2) Implement eviction-wakeup jitter (10-100ms) in branch:evict-jitter and run A/B.
3) Add a lightweight metric: tenant-burst-coincidence-score to console dashboards so oncall can quickly triage alignment issues.
4) Draft PR for residency-manager lock sharding plan (design doc 1 pager).

Notes to self / stray observations:
- The oscillation shape is reminiscent of feedback-control instability; we should avoid manual heuristics only (long-term controller idea warranted).
- Customer communication: prepare a short incident briefing but hold until we have bench confirmation that jitter reduces amplitude.
- This doc is messy. Will clean and move canonical results into CON-8241 once we settle on candidate mitigations.

Appendix (quick traces excerpts):
- evictor traces show sleep-wake cycles: wake(delta) = [42ms, 18ms, 9ms, 4ms, 12ms] preceding the big evict -- suggests cascading triggers rather than a single mistaken large reclaim.
- sample log lines:
  [13:17:34.123] evictor: started batch n=10240 resident=52GB reclaim_target=12GB
  [13:17:34.124] residency: lock_acquire t=34us lock_hold=1.2ms keys=10240
  [13:17:34.498] nvme: read 18.3GB/s window=380ms io-lat-99=9.2ms

If you're looking at this and want to run the bench locally: ping me in #serving-runtime and I'll hand off the branch and harness config.

-- Maya 2025-11-12
